components.name: Button Line

components.name: Form Input
components.description: Single-line text field with film background, ultramarine focus.
components.css: .ds-form-field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 7px; } .ds-form-field label > span { display: block; font-size: 0.88rem; font-weight: 620; color: #0c0e12; } .ds-form-field input { width: 100%; font: inherit; font-size: 1rem; color: #0c0e12; padding: 12px 13px; border: 1px solid #8f9aa6; border-radius: 0; background-color: #eef1f3; transition: border-color 0.2s, background-color 0.2s; } .ds-form-field input:hover { border-color: #56606d; } .ds-form-field input:focus { outline: 2px solid #1e2acb; outline-offset: -1px; border-color: #1e2acb; background-color: #fbfcfd; }

components.name: Title Block Cell
components.description: Credential display in drafting title-block grid (4-column, 2px gaps).
components.css: .ds-tblock { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(4, minmax(0, 1fr)); grid-auto-flow: dense; gap: 1px; margin: 0; border: 2px solid #0c0e12; background-color: #0c0e12; } .ds-tblock > div { display: flex; flex-direction: column; justify-content: space-between; gap: 18px; min-height: 132px; padding: 14px 18px 18px; background-color: #fbfcfd; } .ds-tblock dt { color: #56606d; font-size: 0.72rem; font-weight: 400; margin: 0; } .ds-tblock dd { margin: 0; font-size: 1.15rem; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.3; }

components.name: Demo UI (Wireframe to Rendered)
components.description: Transition using --r (render progress 0–1). Lines fade to color, content fades in.
components.css: .ds-ui { --k: calc(var(--r, 1) * 100%); height: 100%; display: flex; flex-direction: column; font-size: 13px; line-height: 1.35; color: color-mix(in srgb, #0c0e12 var(--k), transparent); background-color: color-mix(in srgb, #fbfcfd var(--k), transparent); border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, #c3cbd3 var(--k), #4e9fd0); border-radius: 0; box-shadow: 0 calc(22px * var(--r, 1)) calc(44px * var(--r, 1)) -20px rgb(12 14 18 / calc(0.32 * var(--r, 1))); } .ds-ui-bar { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: baseline; gap: 12px; padding: 11px 14px; border-bottom: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, #c3cbd3 var(--k), #4e9fd0); } .ds-ui-bar b { font-weight: 740; font-stretch: 112%; font-size: 14px; color: color-mix(in srgb, #0c0e12 var(--k), transparent); } .ds-ui-body { flex: 1; padding: 14px; }

components.name: Navigation
components.description: Fixed 72px nav, transparent on load, solid on scroll. Responsive hamburger at 899px.
components.css: .ds-nav { position: fixed; inset: 0 0 auto; z-index: 50; height: 72px; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 36px; padding: 0 clamp(16px, 5vw, 72px); transition: background-color 0.3s, box-shadow 0.3s; background-color: transparent; } .ds-nav.is-solid { background-color: #eef1f3; box-shadow: 0 1px 0 #c3cbd3; } .ds-logo { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; text-decoration: none; color: #0c0e12; } .ds-logo-mark { width: 34px; height: 34px; } .ds-logo-word { height: 25px; width: auto; aspect-ratio: 645.67 / 152.47; fill: currentColor; }

narrative.overview: Draveta's interface is a blueprint sheet where software construction happens in real time. Everything draws from first principles—geometry, datum lines, measurement callouts—before ink fills and color arrives. The visitor watches the company's own mark assemble from arcs and compass circles, then product interfaces render on the same construction lines. This isn't metaphorical slowness; lines move at constant pen speed, then the finished drawing solidifies. The world refuses the SaaS category default: no rounded cards, no icon tiles, no glass, no gradient overlays. Instead, hairline frames with dimension ticks, a paper-and-ink material, and ultramarine as the single committed color that owns the whole field when action matters.
keyCharacteristics: Drafting paper aesthetic (grid background, construction geometry, measurement callouts)
Square corners and hairline borders throughout; rounding only on device frames (the phone demos) and status dots
Progressive build: lines draw, then ink fills, then color arrives
Ultramarine as the sole high-saturation accent; used sparingly and forcefully
Motion grammar: stroke-dashoffset drawing at constant speed, exponential ease-out, reduced motion shows finished state
Pen-plotter metaphor: the loader splits along the mark's 45° diagonal; the hero pins and scrubs construction/render progress on scroll

rules.name: The Ultramarine Law
rules.body: Ultramarine is the site's only saturated accent and the signal for 'built' and 'action'. It appears on CTAs (buttons, links), the entire products section, the loader, and active form states. No ultramarine in neutral prose or the film grid; line art in the services list is the one illustrative use. It is never decoration.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: All borders are 1px except section dividers (2px) and button registration marks (1.5px). No border-radius anywhere; corners are square. This is the drafting aesthetic: frames are drawn with a straight edge and a compass, not rounded.

rules.name: The Weight Ramp Rule
rules.body: Mona Sans weight is never static in the hero: it starts at 200 (hairline) as the loader finishes, then climbs through 620 during the first ~2.9 seconds as the mark finishes construction. All other type on the page is fixed weight. Only the hero injects motion into weight; the rest of the system is steady.

rules.name: The Mono Law
rules.body: Martian Mono appears only on measurement callouts, inside the loader readout, on data tables, in form labels, and inside demo UI boxes (wireframes transitioning to rendered). Never use it for body prose or primary messaging. Its single job is to convey precision and engineering.

dos: Use the three-layer color order: drafting film (ground), construction blue (geometry), ink + ultramarine (finish).
Keep borders hairline (1px) and corners square (0 radius) on all UI elements except the scanner phone device frame (30px radius only).
Animate SVG strokes using stroke-dasharray: 1 and stroke-dashoffset driven by CSS variables (--a, --s, --r), not SVG animations or JS transitions.
Make ultramarine decisions sparingly: CTAs, product section, loader, active states only. Never tint it or use it decoratively.
Use Martian Mono strictly for measurements, codes, data, and internal UI labels. Never use it for body prose or primary messaging.
Respect reduced-motion preference: show the finished drawing (all strokes at offset 0, all opacity at 1) and hide timing-based animations (duration 0.01ms).
Keep button text uppercase via font-weight and font-stretch, never text-transform: uppercase (preserves user select-and-copy).
Size type fluidly with clamp() for hero, section heads, and key labels; it scales from mobile to 4K without breakpoints.
donts: Don't add glass, blurred backgrounds, or glows beyond the render sweep line; the only drop shadow is the soft offset one on rendered demo panels and the nav product panel.
Don't round corners anywhere except the phone device mockup (30px).
Don't use gradients, transparency overlays, or color blends in the palette itself.
Don't use icon fonts, emoji, or decorative illustration on the UI layer (the knot and loader geometry are drafting-plane elements, not components).
Don't animate through JavaScript; use CSS custom properties and CSS transitions/keyframes.
Don't place ultramarine on neutral prose or use it in tints for fill states. Ultramarine only signals action, construction, and the built state.
Don't invent new type scales or weight assignments; the hierarchy is the hierarchy.
Don't use the fine grid (24px) or construction blue for UI elements; those are drafting-plane backdrop, never component styling.
